answer.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ. Memory_91 demonstrated that in-product activation messaging improved week-one engagement and drove first meaningful action. Memory_86 showed onboarding improvements lift adoption. These are directly addressable levers without the churn risk of memory_73 (deep discounting caused 12-point renewal churn increase) or the scope limitations of enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44 is valuable but wouldn't address broad SMB activation decline). Referral incentives (memory_57) work for established customers but won't solve activation problems in the funnel. Activation messaging offers a targeted, lower-risk intervention that can be tested at standard scale, measured quickly, and rolled back safely. It preserves the option to pivot to onboarding simplification (memory_31) if needed, and avoids promotional pricing which would harm unit economics without addressing the root activation problem.
